reasoning: The flagged scripts (install-user-space.sh, upgrade.sh, remote-install.sh) are not executed during makepkg/build/install. They appear to be standalone utilities not referenced in PKGBUILD or .install scripts. Core packaging files (PKGBUILD, .install) show no malicious behavior.
disagreement_analysis: qwen incorrectly treated standalone scripts as build/install risks. deepseek correctly contextualized them as non-executed during packaging.
coverage_issues: Both models missed contextual analysis of script execution paths
false_positives: install-user-space.sh: Privilege escalation claim ignores script isn't called by PKGBUILD/.install
upgrade.sh: Untrusted copy claim irrelevant to AUR build process
remote-install.sh: Remote download risk doesn't affect package installation
learnings: Prioritize files referenced in PKGBUILD functions (build(), package()) and .install scripts
Improve context awareness: Distinguish between build-time scripts vs unused source files
Add execution path validation to reduce false positives on non-invoked scripts
Enhance variable expansion analysis to avoid overflagging heredocs
